---
title: "check-swallowed-citations.yml"
---

Diff-scoped check that flags a citation
that an in-text cross-reference just before it swallows.
Pandoc reads an in-text citation followed by a bracket
as one citation with a suffix, as in `@key [p. 3]`,
and it reads a Quarto cross-reference such as `@eq-x` with the same grammar.
So the bracket becomes part of the cross-reference,
and the cited source drops out of the rendered page with no warning
(Morrison-Lab/lds#3239).

Flagged:

```markdown
The layer follows @eq-recurrent-layer
[@pascanu2014construct, section 3.3.2].
```

Preferred:

```markdown
The layer follows @eq-recurrent-layer,
as in [@pascanu2014construct, section 3.3.2].
```

`quarto pandoc -t native` (Quarto 1.10) parses the flagged form
as one `Cite` that holds both ids,
and the preferred form as two.

## What it flags

In `.qmd` and `.md` files,
an in-text cross-reference
(`@fig-`, `@tbl-`, `@eq-`, `@sec-`, `@def-`, `@thm-`, `@exm-`,
and the other Quarto prefixes)
followed by a bracket that holds a citation
(`[@key]`, `[-@key]`, `[see @key, p. 3]`).
Only spaces may sit between the two,
or one line break, since the notes break lines at clauses.

## What it does not flag

- a cross-reference followed by punctuation,
  as in `@eq-x, [@key]` or `@eq-x. [@key]`,
  since the punctuation ends the citation;
- a cross-reference inside a bracket, as in `[@eq-x] [@key]`;
- a bracket that is a link, `[@key](url)`, a span, or a reference link;
- a bracket that holds no citation;
- an ordinary citation followed by a bracket, as in `@key [@other]`;
- a blank line between the two, since a paragraph break ends the citation;
- code fences and code spans, HTML comments, and YAML front matter;
- a line carrying, or following,
  `<!-- check-swallowed-citations: allow: <reason> -->`.
  The reason is required.

## Scope

Only lines a pull request adds are reported,
so existing pages never block.
A finding is reported on the line holding the bracket,
and it counts as added when either that line
or the cross-reference's line is one the diff adds.
An added line whose exact text was also deleted in the same diff
counts as moved rather than new.

With no `base-ref`, or when the diff cannot be computed
(a shallow clone, an unresolvable ref),
the check skips with a warning.
It never falls back to a whole-tree scan.
Set `whole-tree: true` to scan every tracked file in full on purpose.

Every run prints how many lines and files it examined.

The check blocks by default,
because the defect is silent in the render
and the pattern has no use a word or a comma cannot serve.
A whole-tree run on 2026-11-28 found 6 hits in lds,
1 each in mds, pds, and mcs,
and none in sds, psw, or psc.
Each hit read by hand was a dropped citation.

## Limitations

- A cross-reference with a prefix outside the Quarto list is not recognized.
- A bracket that spans a line break is not matched.
- A brand new untracked file is invisible to `git diff`.
  Stage it to have a local run examine it.

## Inputs

| Input            | Type    | Default | Description |
| ---------------- | ------- | ------- | ----------- |
| `globs`          | string  | `'*.qmd *.md'` | Space-separated git pathspecs of tracked files to check (recursive by default). |
| `paths-ignore`   | string  | `''`    | Comma- or newline-separated glob patterns (relative paths) to skip. Supports `*`, `?` and recursive `**`. |
| `fail`           | boolean | `true`  | Fail the workflow when a swallowed citation is found. |
| `whole-tree`     | boolean | `false` | Scan every tracked file in full instead of only a PR's added lines. |
| `python-version` | string  | `'3.x'` | Python version to set up. |
| `runs-on` | string | empty (`CI_RUNNER` variable, else `ubuntu-latest`) | Runner label for the job. Use a self-hosted label only for a private repository, because [a public repository's pull requests can run arbitrary code on it](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1167). |

## Permissions

Only `contents: read` (the default), so no `permissions:` block is needed.

## Example

```yaml
# Copy to .github/workflows/check-swallowed-citations.yml in your repo.
# Diff-scoped check: flags a line a PR adds where an in-text cross-reference
# swallows the citation after it, such as "as in @eq-x [@key, section 3]",
# which Pandoc reads as one citation, so @key drops out of the page.
# Fails by default.
# Only contents:read is needed (the default), so no permissions block is required.
name: Check swallowed citations

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  check:
    uses: Morrison-Lab/gha/.github/workflows/check-swallowed-citations.yml@v3
    # with:
    #   globs: '*.qmd *.md'                     # pathspecs to check (recursive)
    #   paths-ignore: 'chapters/outtakes/**'    # skip known-noisy paths
    #   fail: false                             # warn only (defaults to true)
    #   whole-tree: true                        # scan every line, not just a PR's additions
```

See
[`examples/check-swallowed-citations.yml`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/blob/main/examples/check-swallowed-citations.yml)
for the full caller stub.
